waveOwnership: new docs/specs/tests only; no runtime visual mutation

decisions.statement: Mazer's target product is the Fawxzzy Precision Arcade direction: a mobile-first, installable, precision-arcade maze game where the board is the hero and application chrome only explains, enables, or protects play.

Phaser owns world/maze simulation-facing presentation (board rendering, title path animation, world-space entities, camera/world effects, menu demonstration maze, world diagnostics). DOM owns application shell, forms, HUD, touch controls, settings, dialogs, guide/confirmations, and system chrome. Semantic tokens, state registry, commands, view models, responsive metrics, platform profiles, topology/path geometry, icon definitions, motion semantics, diagnostics schema, and capture IDs are shared contracts owned by neither renderer alone.

The shipping maze presentation remains connected corridors, not exposed square tiles. Tile topology stays canonical underlying data; visible square-tile boundaries are optional proof/debug treatment only, never the shipping default.
Mobile, desktop, TV, OBS, arcade, and cyberdeck are output profiles, not public themes. Profiles vary layout and density; they never vary brand identity.

One canonical player-facing theme (Fawxzzy Precision Arcade) replaces the public theme matrix. The noir, ember, vellum, aurora, and monolith theme variants are archived historical experiments, not live public options, and no public theme switch ships in the canonical product.
proof-surfaces.html and visual-proof.html remain internal verification tools (projection QA / critical internal verification), not public product, and are not release-gating core surfaces.

Watch Pass (watch-pass-setup.html, watch-pass-preview.html) remains an incubating companion product behind a feature boundary. watch-pass-paywall.html is a commerce prototype only; no production billing or entitlement claim is permitted until real billing exists.
planet3d.html is an isolated lab, explicitly excluded from core-v1 release acceptance.
future-phaser.html is slated for adapter-lesson extraction (its useful adapter contracts become tests) and then entrypoint retirement.

MenuScene.ts is decomposed through characterization and adapters across later waves, not replaced in one rewrite. A big-bang rewrite is rejected because core scene ownership is migration-sensitive and mechanics are already proof-backed.

The former PR #83 and PR #131 implementation vehicles are superseded. Shared UI and authentication paths are no longer held behind a branch-specific exception; each path may change only in its currently active integrator wave, resolved from an explicit per-wave dependency graph (not one total ordering), with a fresh current-main preflight and exclusive active-writer ownership. A wave's own historical (completed) ownership of a path never grants it permission to keep changing that path after an explicit handoff to a new active owner; two waves with no dependency relationship to each other (e.g. an auth-domain wave and a renderer wave that both merely depend on the same prior wave) may hold active ownership of different paths at once without a dependency edge being invented between them.

Wave 2A introduces only stateless, renderer-neutral DOM construction primitives. These modules own native semantics, accessibility, and primitive styling but do not import MenuScene, authentication, stores, commands, network clients, persistence, or runtime state; they remain unmounted until a later assigned integrator wave.

Wave 2A.1 extends the unmounted DOM foundation with controlled settings rows, sections, switches, radio segments, native scroll ownership, nonblocking status, and safe-default confirmation primitives. Persistence, commands, runtime mounting, provider access, and product appearance remain owned by later integrator waves.

No source lane may claim the redesign complete until the final acceptance matrix (the nine-point Definition of Complete) passes and old duplicated UI paths are removed or formally retained with an owner and purpose.

phaserOwns: world-space player, start, goal, trail, cues, and future Fragment entities

integratorWaveOwnership.modeNote: Each assignment declares its own dependsOn (an array of prerequisite wave ids), not a position in one shared total order -- a wave with no dependency relationship to another may be active at the same time, over different paths, without a dependency edge between them. status distinguishes completed (historical record; no longer enforceable as active ownership of its paths) from active (the current, single, exclusive writer for its paths). Exactly one assignment may be status:'active' for any given path at a time; multiple completed assignments may reference the same path as history (a real handoff), which is not a violation.

assignments.completionNote: PR #343, squash-merged to main. Made the Wave 1A shared UI command/state contracts load-bearing against the real running scene. src/scenes/MenuScene.ts's active ownership hands off to Wave 4D-A below (Navigation Core runtime); src/state/uiLegacyBridge.ts has no active claimant after this handoff and is available to a future wave that needs it.

assignments.note: Implements the frozen docs/assets/reference/navigation-core-v1/ visual authority into the real Phaser runtime. Depends only on Wave 3A's completion (the command bridge it builds on top of); no dependency edge to Wave 3B is required or implied -- the two waves own disjoint paths and neither's work gates the other. src/render/navigationCoreTrail.ts is a new pure geometry/color/shine module extracted out of MenuScene.ts for the continuous trail (arc-length path building, corner rounding, energy-palette color sampling, shared shine timing) -- added here explicitly rather than left unowned. src/render/navigationCoreTrailCanvas.ts is a second new module claimed here: a real 2D-canvas compositor for the same trail (continuous multi-point stroke chunks with real line joins, plus a genuine shadowBlur-based glow), replacing Graphics vector strokes once those proved unable to avoid a corner self-intersection artifact -- this game runs Phaser.CANVAS, so Phaser's WebGL-only postFX/preFX blur was never an available alternative. src/scenes/BootScene.ts is also claimed here: it gained a load-bearing derived-texture generator (the floor-tile interior crop the corridor material depends on) as part of this same visual authority, with a failure-safe fallback that disables the floor-texture accent rather than ever showing Phaser's missing-texture placeholder or the raw bordered source.

integratorWaveOwnership.note: Assignments preserve the handoff packet's single-owner guardrails while replacing the obsolete pull-request hold with current dependency-graph wave ownership. The Wave 1B token exports are concrete and assigned. Wave 2A's base DOM primitives and Wave 2A.1's settings extensions remain stateless and unwired; no branch name or stale pull-request state grants an exception.
